preamble: Debuccalization of the velar ejective: [kʼ] loses its oral closure and keeps only the glottal one, giving [ʔ]. Fallon (2002) counts this among the most frequent ejective changes, attested as regular or dialectal change in Chadic, Cushitic, Omotic, Athabaskan and Jicaquean. Several cases are still variable between dialects, showing the change in progress. In Maltese, as in Cairene and urban Levantine Arabic, the same endpoint is reached via uvular q (*kʼ > q > ʔ).

examples.note: Word-initial ƙ only (Dresel 1977, cited in Fallon 2002).
Western Jicaque kat instead lost the glottalization (Campbell & Oltrogge 1980).
Still spelled q; may be inherited from Sicilian Arabic or independent.
